//: Type-checking for a .jsx codebase, via JSDoc rather than a file rename.
checkJs + allowJs means `tsc --noEmit` type-checks the existing .js files
using their JSDoc annotations. No file is renamed, no import path changes,
the Vite build is untouched (esbuild still does the transpiling), and
finance.test.js / instruments.test.js keep working as they are. Renaming to
.ts would have bought stricter guarantees at the cost of touching every
import site and leaving the tree half .ts and half .jsx.
`include` is deliberately narrow and grows as each area is annotated. A
tsconfig that covers everything on day one reports thousands of errors, and
the only way to get CI green is to relax the compiler until it says nothing
-- which is how a type-check gate ends up proving nothing. These are the
money-adjacent modules, which is where an undefined property costs real
value: finance.js does the Decimal arithmetic, instruments.js decides what
may be traded, services/api.js shapes every payload, store/useStore.js holds
Widen it by adding a path here, fixing what it reports, and committing both
together. `npm run typecheck` is a blocking CI step, so it may only grow.
